caption:
Mr Turtle got new varifocals, and now his chin keeps tilting up to read the screen.

In varifocals the lower part of the lens is usually for close-up, so a high monitor can mean looking up through the bottom of the lens. Hold that for hours and the back of the neck often feels stiff.

Hybi's set-up: lower the monitor a little, sit about an arm's length away, and do chin tucks (5 seconds × 5) every 30 minutes. Your optometrist can advise on dedicated computer glasses.

Frequent headaches, arm tingling or no change after two weeks are worth an assessment. Our Chatswood and Sydney CBD physios can help. Book online via the link in bio 👓
